questions.question: By how much has the grant for National Championships in high-priority sports been increased, as per the 2025 announcement?

__
 
• In a significant move to bolster the domestic sports ecosystem, the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of **India**, announced a revised financial assistance structure in early **2025**.
 
• As per the **2025** announcement, the grant for organizing **National Championships** in the **High-Priority sports** category has been increased to **₹90 lakh**.
 
• Previously, the financial assistance for this category was capped at **₹51 lakh**, marking an increase of approximately **76%** to ensure better facilities and competitive standards.
 
• For the **Priority sports** category, the grant has been enhanced from **₹30 lakh** to **₹75 lakh**, representing a substantial **150%** jump in funding.
 
• For the **Other sports** category (categorized as 'Others'), the assistance for conducting **National Championships** has been raised from **₹22 lakh** to **₹30 lakh**.
 
• This decision is part of the broader **Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs)**, aimed at professionalizing the conduct of national-level tournaments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs):**
 
 
• This is a flagship central scheme that provides financial support to **NSFs** for training and participation of **Indian** athletes in international competitions.
 
• It covers the cost of **National Coaching Camps**, foreign exposures, equipment purchase, and the salary of **National Coaches**.
 
• The revision in **2025** reflects the government's commitment to the **Vision 2047** for sports, focusing on grassroots development and podium finishes.
 
 
 
• **Categorization of Sports:**
 
 
• **High-Priority:** Includes disciplines like **Athletics**, **Archery**, **Boxing**, **Shooting**, **Wrestling**, and **Badminton** where **India** has strong medal prospects at the **Olympics** and **Asian Games**.
 
• **Priority:** Includes sports that are part of the **Olympics**, **Asian Games**, or **Commonwealth Games** but require further development to reach world-class levels.
 
• **Others:** Includes sports that are recognized by the **Ministry** but are not currently part of the major multi-sport international events.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** has also increased the remuneration for support staff and **coaches** to attract and retain high-quality talent within the **Indian** sports system.
 
• The enhancement of grants for **National Championships** is expected to encourage **NSFs** to host events in **Tier-2** and **Tier-3** cities, thereby increasing the **geographical reach** of various sports.
 
• The **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** plays a pivotal role in monitoring the utilization of these funds and ensuring that the benefits reach the **athletes** directly.
 
• This funding boost is timed strategically as **India** prepares for the **2026 Asian Games** and looks forward to the **2028 Los Angeles Olympics**.

questions.question: Who became the first Thai male badminton player to be ranked World No. 1 in men’s singles in May 2025?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kunlavut Vitidsarn** made history in **May 2025** by becoming the first male player from **Thailand** to reach the **World No. 1** spot in the **BWF World Rankings** for the men’s singles category.
 
• His rise to the top of the global rankings followed a period of exceptional consistency on the **BWF World Tour** and major international championships.
 
• One of his most significant career milestones was winning the **Gold Medal** at the **2023 BWF World Championships** held in **Copenhagen**, where he defeated Kodai Naraoka in the final.
 
• He further solidified his standing as a global badminton icon by securing a **Silver Medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympic Games**, marking a historic achievement for **Thai badminton**.
 
• Before his senior success, he was a dominant force in the junior circuit, becoming the first male player to win **three consecutive World Junior Championship** titles in **2017, 2018, and 2019**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Badminton World Federation (BWF) Ranking System**:
 
 
• The **World No. 1** ranking is determined by the total points accumulated by a player in their **top 10 tournament results** over the preceding **52 weeks**.
 
• Achieving this rank requires deep runs into high-level tournaments such as **Super 750** and **Super 1000** events.
 
 
 
• **Other Candidates in the Options**:
 
 
• **Lee Zii Jia**: A prominent player from **Malaysia** who reached a career-high of **World No. 2** and won the prestigious **All England Open** in **2021**.
 
• **Kento Momota**: A legendary former **World No. 1** from **Japan** who holds the record for the most titles won in a single season (**11 titles in 2019**).
 
• **Kantaphon Wangcharoen**: A fellow **Thai** player who became the first Thai man to win a medal (**Bronze**) at the **BWF World Championships** in **2019**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context**: While **Ratchanok Intanon** became the first Thai player to reach **World No. 1** in the women’s singles category in **2016**, **Kunlavut Vitidsarn** is the first to do so in the men’s division, completing a major milestone for the sport in **Thailand**.
 
• **Training Background**: Kunlavut trains at the **Banthongyod Badminton School** in **Bangkok**, the same academy that produced former world champion Ratchanok Intanon.
 
• **Playing Style**: Known by his nickname **"View,"** his game is characterized by exceptional **defensive skills**, net play precision, and high **stamina**, which allows him to outlast aggressive power hitters.
 
• **Age and Career Peak**: Born in **May 2001**, reaching the **World No. 1** position at age **24** in **2025** represents the peak of his physical and tactical development.

questions.question: According to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change’s official release dated 1 September 2025 titled “In the last 8 years, Delhi witnesses best AQI figures in 2025 for the January–August period”, what was Delhi’s average AQI during January–August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**172**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, **Delhi** recorded its best average **Air Quality Index (AQI)** for the **January–August** period in **2025**, with a value of **172**.
 
• This data was highlighted in an official release dated **1 September 2025**, titled “In the last 8 years, Delhi witnesses best AQI figures in 2025 for the January–August period”.
 
• The average **AQI** of **172** in **2025** is a significant improvement compared to the same period in previous years: it was **187** in **2024**, **174** in **2023**, and **194** in **2022**.
 
• This figure represents the lowest average **AQI** for the first eight months of the year since **2018**, excluding the outlier year of **2020**, which saw drastic reductions in pollution due to the **COVID-19** lockdown.
 
• The improvement reflects the impact of sustained efforts and various policy interventions implemented to curb air pollution in the **National Capital Region (NCR)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 172.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Air Quality Index (AQI):**

 
 
• The **AQI** is a numerical scale used by government agencies to communicate to the public how polluted the air currently is or how polluted it is forecast to become.
 
• In **India**, the **National Air Quality Index** was launched in **October 2014** to provide "One Number- One Colour-One Description" for the common man to judge the air quality.
 
• The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** monitors and calculates the **AQI** based on eight major pollutants: **PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, and Pb**.
 
 
 
• **AQI Categories:**
 
 
• The index is divided into six categories: **Good (0–50)**, **Satisfactory (51–100)**, **Moderately Polluted (101–200)**, **Poor (201–300)**, **Very Poor (301–400)**, and **Severe (401–500)**.
 
• An average of **172** falls within the **'Moderately Polluted'** category, which may cause breathing discomfort to people with lungs, asthma, and heart diseases.
 
 
 
• **Pollution Control Measures in Delhi:**
 
 
• The **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)** in **NCR** and Adjoining Areas is responsible for the overall strategy to tackle pollution.
 
• The **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)** is a set of emergency measures that kick in to prevent further deterioration of air quality in **Delhi-NCR** based on different **AQI** thresholds.
 
• Initiatives such as the promotion of **Electric Vehicles (EVs)**, shifting to **PNG (Piped Natural Gas)** in industries, and dust management at construction sites have contributed to the downward trend in **AQI** levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparative Data:**

 
 
• In **2024**, the average **AQI** for the **January–August** period was **187**.
 
• In **2023**, the average **AQI** for the same period was **174**.
 
• The **2025** data shows a decrease in the concentration of **Particulate Matter (PM2.5 and PM10)**, which are the primary concerns for **Delhi's** air quality.
 
 
 
• **Meteorological Factors:**
 
 
• Apart from government policy, meteorological factors such as **rainfall** and **wind speed** during the **Monsoon** and summer months play a crucial role in determining the average **AQI**.
 
• The **Ministry of Environment** noted that the number of 'Good' to 'Moderate' air quality days has been steadily increasing over the last few years due to both favorable weather and strict enforcement of environmental laws.

questions.question: In June 2025, Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) joint venture NISAR is planned to be launched by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GSLV Mk II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **NISAR** (**NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar**) is a joint Earth-observing mission between the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and the **National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)**.
 
• The mission is scheduled to be launched in **June 2025** from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)** located in **Sriharikota**, **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The primary launch vehicle designated for this mission is the **GSLV Mk II** (**Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mark II**), which is a three-stage heavy-lift vehicle developed by **ISRO**.
 
• **NISAR** will be the first satellite mission to use two different radar frequencies, the **L-band** and the **S-band**, to measure changes in our planet's surface less than a centimeter across.
 
• The **L-band SAR** (Synthetic Aperture Radar) is provided by **NASA**’s **Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)**, while **ISRO** has developed the **S-band SAR**, the spacecraft bus, and the launch services.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is GSLV Mk II**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **GSLV Mk II (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mark II):**
 
 
• The **GSLV Mk II** is the largest launch vehicle currently in operational use by **India**, featuring a **Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS)**.
 
• It is a **4th generation** launch vehicle designed to place satellites into **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)** and **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.
 
• The vehicle has a payload capacity of approximately **2,500 kg** to **GTO** and up to **5,000 kg** to **LEO**.
 
 
 
• **NISAR Mission Objectives:**
 
 
• The mission aims to observe **Earth’s land and ice surfaces** globally with unprecedented precision to understand **climate change**, **ecosystem disturbances**, and **natural hazards**.
 
• It will map the entire globe in **12 days** and provide spatially and temporally consistent data for understanding changes in **Earth’s ecosystems**, **ice mass**, and **natural disasters** like **earthquakes**, **tsunamis**, **volcanoes**, and **landslides**.
 
• The data will also support **agricultural monitoring**, **groundwater management**, and tracking the rate of **sea-level rise**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NASA-ISRO Partnership:** This collaboration represents a landmark agreement between **India** and the **United States** in the field of space exploration, signed in **2014**.
 
• **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR):** Unlike optical sensors, **SAR** can penetrate **clouds** and **darkness**, allowing the satellite to collect data day and night, regardless of weather conditions.
 
• **Mission Life:** The **NISAR** mission has a planned duration of at least **3 years**, during which it will provide critical data to the scientific community for **global environmental research**.
 
• **Budget and Logistics:** The total cost of the mission is estimated to be around **1.5 billion USD**, making it one of the world's most expensive **Earth-imaging** satellites.

questions.question: According to the World Bank’s Global Economic Prospects (June 2025), global growth is projected to slow markedly to what percentage in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.3%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **World Bank’s** flagship report titled **Global Economic Prospects** released in **June 2025**, the global economy is expected to witness a significant deceleration.
 
• The report projects that **global growth** will slow markedly to **2.3%** in **2025**, reflecting the ongoing impact of tight **monetary policies** and restrictive **credit conditions**.
 
• This growth rate of **2.3%** is a downward revision compared to earlier optimistic projections, highlighting the fragility of the post-pandemic recovery. ***Hence, the correct option is 2.3%.***
 
• The **World Bank** identifies persistent **inflation**, high **interest rates**, and reduced **fiscal support** as the primary drivers behind this cooling of the global economic engine.
 
• Economic activity in **Advanced Economies** is expected to remain subdued, while **Emerging Markets and Developing Economies (EMDEs)** face challenges related to high **debt levels** and sluggish **investment** growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The World Bank:** 
 
 
• Established in **1944** at the **Bretton Woods Conference**, the World Bank is an international financial institution that provides loans and grants to the governments of low- and middle-income countries.
 
• It is headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, and operates with the primary goal of **reducing poverty** and promoting **shared prosperity** across the globe.
 
 
 
• **Global Economic Prospects (GEP) Report:**
 
 
• The **GEP** is a semi-annual report published by the World Bank, typically in **January** and **June**, examining global economic developments and prospects.
 
• The report provides essential data for **policymakers**, **investors**, and **academics** to understand the trajectory of **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** and **trade** cycles.
 
 
 
• **Economic Terminologies:**
 
 
• **GDP Growth:** The annual percentage growth rate of **GDP** at market prices based on constant local currency.
 
• **Monetary Tightening:** A policy implemented by **Central Banks** (like the **Federal Reserve** or **RBI**) to reduce the money supply and curb **inflation**, often by raising **benchmark interest rates**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **June 2025** report emphasizes that **geopolitical tensions** and **trade fragmentation** are significant **downside risks** that could further dampen growth below the **2.3%** mark.
 
• For many **developing nations**, the projected slowdown poses a threat to **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, as lower growth limits the resources available for **education**, **healthcare**, and **infrastructure**.
 
• The **World Bank** urges **global cooperation** to address **debt distress** in low-income countries and to accelerate the **energy transition** to mitigate long-term economic risks.

questions.question: As per the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth for 2025-26 is projected for Q4 at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.5%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meeting held in **December 2024**, provided the first set of projections for the **fiscal year 2025-26 (FY26)**.
 
• As per the **RBI**, the **Real Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** growth for **Q4 of 2025-26** is projected to be **6.5%**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 6.5%.***
 
• For the entire **fiscal year 2025-26**, the **RBI** has projected a growth rate of **6.8%**, assuming a normal monsoon and stable global conditions.
 
• The quarterly projections for **FY26** are as follows: **Q1** at **7.2%**, **Q2** at **6.8%**, **Q3** at **6.7%**, and **Q4** at **6.5%**.
 
• These projections are vital for **investors**, **policymakers**, and **businesses** to gauge the health and trajectory of the **Indian economy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**:
 
 
• **GDP** represents the total **monetary value** of all finished goods and services produced within a **country's borders** in a specific time period.
 
• It serves as a comprehensive scorecard of a **country’s economic health** and is calculated by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** in India.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**:
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member** committee constituted by the **Central Government** under **Section 45ZB** of the **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• It is chaired by the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India**, currently **Shaktikanta Das**.
 
• The primary objective of the **MPC** is to maintain **price stability** while keeping in mind the objective of **growth**.
 
 
 
• **Growth Drivers for FY26**:
 
 
• The **RBI** expects growth to be supported by **resilient domestic demand**, a revival in **rural consumption**, and sustained **government capital expenditure**.
 
• The **manufacturing** and **services sectors** continue to be the primary engines of the **Indian economy**, showing robust **Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI)** figures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inflation Targeting**:
 
 
• Along with **GDP projections**, the **RBI** also monitors **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** inflation. The medium-term target for **CPI inflation** is **4%** with a band of **+/- 2%**.

questions.question: In which year did India present its Third Voluntary National Review (VNR) Report on Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India is scheduled to present its **Third Voluntary National Review (VNR)** report on the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** in the year **2025**.
 
• The **VNR** is a process through which countries assess and present progress made in achieving the **17 Sustainable Development Goals** and the pledge to leave no one behind.
 
• This report will be presented at the **United Nations High-Level Political Forum (HLPF)**, which is the main platform for the follow-up and review of the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**.
 
• **NITI Aayog**, the premier policy think tank of the **Government of India**, is the nodal agency responsible for overseeing the implementation of **SDGs** and preparing the **VNR**.
 
• The **Third VNR** in **2025** will highlight India's efforts in "Accelerating the delivery of sustainable, resilient, and innovative solutions" to overcome global challenges and meet the **2030** deadline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Previous VNRs of India**:
 
 
• **First VNR (2017)**: India presented its inaugural review in **2017**, focusing on early-stage implementation of schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana** and **Swachh Bharat Mission**.
 
• **Second VNR (2020)**: Presented during the **HLPF** in **July 2020**, this report was titled "**Decade of Action: Taking SDGs from Global to Local**," emphasizing the localization of goals across **States** and **Union Territories**.
 
 
 
• **SDG India Index**: To monitor progress domestically, **NITI Aayog** launched the **SDG India Index** in **2018**. It ranks states based on their performance across various social, economic, and environmental indicators.
 
• **The 17 SDGs**: Also known as **Global Goals**, these were adopted by the **United Nations** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure that by **2030** all people enjoy peace and prosperity.
 
• **Global Monitoring**: The **VNRs** aim to facilitate the sharing of experiences, including successes, challenges, and lessons learned, with a view to accelerating the implementation of the **2030 Agenda**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Localization of SDGs**: India has been recognized globally for its efforts in **localizing SDGs** through district-level monitoring and creating a competitive environment among states to achieve targets.
 
• **Viksit Bharat @2047**: India’s progress on **SDGs** is increasingly being aligned with the long-term vision of becoming a developed nation (**Viksit Bharat**) by the **year 2047**, the centenary of its independence.
 
• **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)**: A significant part of the **Third VNR** documentation is expected to focus on how India's **DPI** (like **Aadhaar**, **UPI**, and **Gati Shakti**) has acted as a multiplier for achieving goals related to **Financial Inclusion (Goal 8)** and **Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure (Goal 9)**.
 
• **Climate Action**: India’s commitment to the **Panchamrit** targets announced at **COP26** and its progress toward **Net Zero** by **2070** are central themes in the environmental segment of the **SDG** reviews.

questions.question: In March 2025, a rare long‑snouted vine snake was rediscovered in which of the following national parks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dudhwa National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **March 2025**, a rare **long-snouted vine snake** was rediscovered and documented in the **Dudhwa National Park**, which is located in the **Lakhimpur Kheri** district of **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The **long-snouted vine snake** (belonging to the genus **Ahaetulla**) is an **arboreal** reptile known for its slender body and distinctively **pointed snout**, which aids in its specialized predatory behavior in dense foliage.
 
• This rediscovery is of great ecological significance as the species is rarely sighted in the **Terai-Arc Landscape**, and its presence indicates a thriving and **undisturbed ecosystem** within the park.
 
• The sighting occurred during a specialized **herpetofaunal survey** conducted by **wildlife researchers** and the **Uttar Pradesh Forest Department** to catalog rare reptilian species.
 
• The snake is characterized by its **vivid green color**, which provides excellent **camouflage** among the leaves, making it extremely difficult to spot during routine patrols. ***Hence, the correct answer is Dudhwa National Park.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dudhwa National Park:**
 
 
• It was established as a **National Park** in **January 1977** and covers an area of approximately **490 square kilometers**.
 
• The park is a vital part of the **Dudhwa Tiger Reserve**, which also encompasses the **Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary** and the **Katarniaghat Wildlife Sanctuary** along the **Indo-Nepal border**.
 
• It is renowned for being the last refuge for the **Barasingha** (Swamp Deer) in the **Gangetic plains** and serves as a critical habitat for **Bengal Tigers** and **One-horned Rhinoceros**.
 
• The landscape is dominated by **Sal forests** (Shorea robusta), extensive **marshes**, and **tall grasslands**, typical of the **Terai region**.
 
 
 
• **Vine Snakes (Genus Ahaetulla):**
 
 
• These snakes are **mildly venomous** (rear-fanged) but are generally harmless to humans; their venom is primarily used to immobilize small prey like **lizards** and **frogs**.
 
• They possess **horizontal pupils**, a rare feature among snakes, which provides them with **binocular vision** and excellent depth perception for hunting.
 
• The **long-snouted** variety is specifically adapted to the high-canopy environments of **tropical and sub-tropical forests**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation Status:** The **Terai region** of **Uttar Pradesh** is a high-priority **conservation zone** due to its proximity to the **Himalayan foothills** and its role as a **wildlife corridor** between **India** and **Nepal**.
 
• **Biodiversity Significance:** **Dudhwa National Park** is home to over **450 species of birds**, making it a premier destination for **ornithology** and **ecotourism** in **Northern India**.
 
• **Geographical Context:** The park is influenced by the **Suheli** and **Mohana** rivers, which create the **wetland ecosystem** necessary for the survival of the **endangered** flora and fauna of the region.
 
• **Recent Discoveries:** The **March 2025** discovery of the **vine snake** follows a series of efforts by the **Government of India** to strengthen **biodiversity databases** through the **National Biodiversity Authority**.
</ul

questions.question: In August 2025, the Department of Posts signed a Memorandum of Understanding with which association in an effort to broaden access to mutual fund products, leveraging the trust and reach of post offices across the country?

options.text: All India Association of Mutual Fund Advisors
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
Association of Mutual Funds in India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Association of Mutual Funds in India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **August 2025**, the **Department of Posts** (operating as **India Post**) officially signed a **Memorandum of Understanding** (**MoU**) with the **Association of Mutual Funds in India** (**AMFI**).
 
• The primary objective of this strategic partnership is to broaden the access to **mutual fund** products across the length and breadth of the country, specifically targeting **rural** and **semi-urban** populations.
 
• By leveraging the extensive network of over **1,60,000** **post offices**, the initiative seeks to utilize the high level of **trust** and **last-mile connectivity** that the **postal department** enjoys in India.
 
• This collaboration aims to facilitate **financial inclusion** by providing a simplified and reliable platform for common citizens to invest in **market-linked** financial instruments.
 
• The move is expected to significantly increase the penetration of **Systematic Investment Plans** (**SIPs**) and other **mutual fund** schemes among **retail investors** who previously had limited access to formal **wealth management** services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Department of Posts (India Post):**
 
 
• It functions under the **Ministry of Communications** of the **Government of India**.
 
• Established in **1854** by **Lord Dalhousie**, it has grown into the most widely distributed **postal network** in the world.
 
• Beyond traditional mail, it provides various **financial services** through the **Post Office Savings Bank** (**POSB**), which is one of the oldest and largest **banking systems** in the country.
 
 
 
• **Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI):**
 
 
• **AMFI** is the **apex body** of all **Asset Management Companies** (**AMCs**) in India that are registered with **SEBI**.
 
• It was incorporated on **August 22, 1995**, as a non-profit organization to maintain **professional standards** and ethics in the **mutual fund** industry.
 
• One of its major functions is to promote **investor awareness** through campaigns like "**Mutual Funds Sahi Hai**."
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Oversight:**
 
 
• The **mutual fund** industry in India is regulated by the **Securities and Exchange Board of India** (**SEBI**), established under the **SEBI Act, 1992**.
 
• **SEBI** ensures **transparency**, protects **investor interests**, and monitors the **Net Asset Value** (**NAV**) disclosures of various schemes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Financial Inclusion Goals:** This **MoU** aligns with the **Government of India’s** mission to ensure that **financial services** reach the "**Antyodaya**" (the last person in the queue).
 
• **Reach Statistics:** While **private banks** and **broking firms** are concentrated in **Tier-1** and **Tier-2** cities, **India Post** reaches more than **6,00,000** villages, providing a unique **geographical advantage** for **AMFI** members.
 
• **Diversification:** The introduction of **mutual funds** via **post offices** allows traditional savers to transition from **fixed-income** assets like **Fixed Deposits** (**FDs**) to **equity** and **hybrid** funds, potentially earning higher **inflation-adjusted returns** over the **long term**.
 
• **Trust Factor:** For many **rural** households, the **Postman** or **Gramin Dak Sevak** is a **trusted advisor**, making the adoption of new **financial products** smoother compared to **digital-only** platforms.
